name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the function $f(x)=-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ In **ascending order**, the **exact values** of the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}}
$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
A critical point of $f(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $f$ such that either ${f}^{′}(c)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(c)$ does not exist.

Differentiating $f(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the critical points:

- First, we compute the points where ${f}^{′}(c)=0.$ We set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =0 \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =-\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})+n\pi  \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi <x<\pi .$

- setting $n=0$ gives $x=-\frac{\pi }{3},$

- setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi <x<\pi .$ So, the solutions to this equation for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are 

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{3},\,x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ has stationary points at $x=-\frac{\pi }{3}$ and $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

- Second, we note that ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists for all values of $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ So $f(x)$ has no non-stationary critical points.

Therefore, in ascending order, the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are 

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{and}\,x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
